newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - T-bonds to consolidate, capped at 110-14.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bonds to consolidate, capped at 110-14.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries face a period of choppy trade in the next few days as the market consolidates, technical analysts said on Monday.
Last Friday's high at 110-14 may prove hard to crack on Monday, but must be convincingly vaulted by Friday to open up the potential for further gains.
"We are in a fairly impulsive part of this rally," said analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in a note for clients.
"While we might still be in a second wave correction, and could thus range trade today, to remain bullish beyond that, prices need to push higher by Tuesday."
By 0920 GMT, June T-bonds were down 1/32 at 110-06 in automated trade, off an earlier high of 110-10.
Deutsche said a failure to rally well past 110-14 by Friday, particularly if accompanied by friendly data and a stable dollar, would be a sign that a top is closer than currently anticipated.
Above 110-14, resistance comes in at 110-29, then 111-06, the 50 percent retracement of the whole price drop from 116-00 on December 3 1996 to 106-12 on April 11, they said.
On the downside, 109-16 is key, analysts said. "If we are going to rally to 112-00, we should not retrace deeper than that," said Deutsche. "Set stops on longs just below that level."
Richard Adcock, manager of technical research at HSBC Futures in London, said T-bonds were likely to experience some weakness leading to short-term consolidation.
"Treasuries have performed pretty well in the last few days, but there are some signs of these new highs not being confirmed by momntum indicators," Adcock said.
"They haven't yet given sell signals but if they turn down to do that then the risk is we will enter to a more prolonged consolidation there."
Adcock put resistance around 110-10, then 110-20. He put initial support around 109-26, a congestion area on the way up the chart.
By 0922 GMT, September Eurodollars were down 0.005 at 93.925.
